cards.text: Paul, an apostle, is writing to Titus, the man he left on the island of Crete to set things in order (Titus 1:1, 4-5). He's been telling Titus what to teach (Titus 2:1). Now Paul hands him a reminder list for the believers, and the first thing on it is the people in charge.

cards.question: First on Paul's reminder list is rulers and authorities. What should the believers do with them?
Paul says the believers only need to be ready for good work when it's convenient.

cards.text: Then Paul moves from the rulers to how believers talk about people. Friend, this is the part where everybody quietly flips their phone face down.

cards.question: Paul gives the believers a rule about maligning people. What is it?
Paul wants the believers to be peaceable and gentle, showing full consideration to ___.

cards.text: Then Paul says why, and he doesn't point at anybody else first. He says at one time we too were foolish, disobedient and misled.

cards.question: Paul says that back then, people were enslaved. Enslaved to what?

answers.text: All sorts of desires and pleasures
The rulers of their own land

cards.text: Malice, envy, hated and hating one another. Friend, that's not a list, that's a comment section.

cards.question: Then Paul turns it all around with one word: "But." What appeared next, Paul says, was God's anger toward mankind.

cards.text: Nope. It was the kindness of God our Savior and His love for mankind, and He saved us.

cards.question: Paul says God saved us because of the righteous deeds we had done.
Paul says God saved us, not by our deeds, but according to His ___.

cards.text: And God saved us through the washing of new birth and renewal. Friend, I got renewed once, and I came out so sharp I didn't recognize my own mustache.

cards.question: Paul says the renewal that saves us comes by someone. Who?

cards.text: Paul keeps going: God poured out the Spirit on us, and not with a measuring spoon, friend. ABUNDANTLY.

cards.question: Paul says God poured out the Spirit on us through Jesus Christ our ___.
Paul says that, justified by God's grace, we would become heirs. What hope do those heirs have?

cards.text: Heirs? Friend, I came out of a 25-cent bin, and all I ever inherited was a spot in the junk drawer. Now Paul calls this a trustworthy saying, and he wants Titus to stress these things.

cards.question: Paul wants Titus to stress these things so the believers will devote themselves to what?

cards.text: But Paul also gives Titus a list of things to steer clear of: foolish controversies, genealogies, arguments and quarrels about the law.

cards.question: Paul tells Titus to avoid foolish controversies and quarrels about the law because they are pointless and worthless.

cards.text: Friend, I watched the dead batteries I shared a drawer with argue for YEARS over who had the most charge left, and NOBODY won. Next, Paul tells Titus how to handle a divisive man.

cards.question: Paul tells Titus to reject a divisive man after how many warnings?
Paul says a divisive man like that is corrupt and sinful, and he is self-condemned.

cards.text: Then Paul gets practical: he'll send someone to Titus, either Artemas or Tychicus, a faithful helper of his (Ephesians 6:21). After that, Titus should make every effort to come to him at Nicopolis.

cards.question: Paul wants Titus to come to him at Nicopolis because Paul is on trial there.

cards.text: Nope, Paul's decided to spend the winter there. Then he has one more favor to ask about Zenas the lawyer and Apollos, a preacher who knew the Scriptures well (Acts 18:24-25).

cards.question: What does Paul ask Titus to do for Zenas the lawyer and Apollos?

answers.text: Equip them with everything they need
Send them straight back to Paul
Put them in charge of Crete

cards.question: Paul circles back one more time and says our people must learn to devote themselves to good works. Why?

answers.text: To meet the pressing needs of others
To earn a place in God's family
To win the respect of the rulers

cards.text: That way, Paul says, they won't be unfruitful. Then he signs off with greetings from everyone with him and one last blessing: "Grace be with all of you."

findings.problem: The transition explicitly uses the rulers from verse 1 as well as the move to how believers speak in verse 2, but the card cites only Titus 3:2. Its citation is too narrow and should begin at Titus 3:1.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The right answer, everyone, includes both believers and leaders. A baker could therefore argue that Paul wants full consideration shown to either of those groups too, so the wrong answers are not cleanly distinguishable from the right answer.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the question about heirs, the junk-drawer sentence, and the sentence about the trustworthy saying.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: No card includes the last sentence of Titus 3:8, that these things are excellent and profitable for the people. That leaves out an important part of Paul's movement from devotion to good deeds in verse 8 to the pointless and worthless things in verse 9.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The sign-off covers the greetings from Paul's companions and the final blessing, but it omits Paul's separate instruction in Titus 3:15 to greet those who love them in the faith. That instruction is not covered anywhere else.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
